evidence.claim: Scoped OAuth apps work on other accounts only after publishing
evidence.quote: Publishing is required for an app with Scoped OAuth functionality to work on accounts other than the one that created it.
We aim to review your submission and approve or reply with feedback within 5 business days.

evidence.claim: An admin on each account must install the app
evidence.quote: Before any user on another account can authorize your app, an admin on that account must install it.

evidence.claim: Classic User OAuth works across accounts and has only read/write scopes
evidence.quote: Classic User OAuth, the legacy OAuth functionality, works across accounts regardless of App Type

evidence.claim: The authorize endpoint is live and rejects unknown clients
evidence.note: Returned 400 Client is invalid or unknown.

evidence.claim: App Registration is limited to Manager, Global Admin or Account Owner base roles
evidence.quote: App Registration is available only to users with a base role of Manager, Global Admin or Account Owner.

evidence.note: The docs read did not print the authorize URL. The path was confirmed by the probe.

evidence.claim: Scoped OAuth needs client_secret and PKCE
evidence.quote: A Scoped OAuth app is always a confidential client: it must send its client_secret on the token request and must use PKCE.

evidence.note: Access token 1 day. Rolling window 1 year.

evidence.claim: App token needs an as_account scope in REGION.SUBDOMAIN format
evidence.quote: Must contain the as_account- scope that specifies the PagerDuty Account the token is being requested for using a {REGION}.{SUBDOMAIN} format.

evidence.note: The sample at martindstone.github.io/PDOAuth shows GET api.pagerduty.com/users/me. It was not on a provider page I read.

evidence.claim: docs.pagerduty.com/developer/publish-an-app is the provider's review / go-live page

points: Go to Integrations > Developer Tools > App Registration > New App.

where.label: PagerDuty → Integrations → Developer Tools → App Registration

points: On the app's Edit App page, click Add on the OAuth card.
Choose Scoped OAuth.
Enter your app's OAuth callback URL, then pick the scopes.
steps.title: Add Scoped OAuth, callback URL and scopes

where.label: PagerDuty → App Registration → Edit App → Functionality

points: Send the user to the authorize URL with code_challenge (S256).
Exchange the code at the token URL with client_secret and code_verifier.
Store the client secret only with the developer's OK.
Refresh user tokens before the 30-day refresh expiry.
steps.title: Run the authorization code flow with PKCE

points: Draft the listing documentation using PagerDuty's documentation template.
Write the support contact and testing instructions.
steps.title: Prepare the Distribution Form materials

where.label: PagerDuty → Edit App → App Type → Distribution Form

points: Select Public, complete the Distribution Form, then Save and confirm.
The app can't be edited after submission. Email apps@pagerduty.com to reopen it.
steps.title: Set App Type to Public and submit for review

points: PagerDuty aims to respond within 5 business days.
Reviewers may ask for changes.
steps.title: Wait for PagerDuty review

points: Give each admin the install link.
Users can authorize only after the install.
steps.title: Have customer admins install the app

points: GET https://api.pagerduty.com/users/me with Authorization: Bearer <access_token>.
Success is a 200 with the user's JSON. A 401 means the token expired. A 403 means a missing scope.

uncertainties.text: Authorization code lifetime is not stated on the pages read.
Exact redirect URI rules (exact match, HTTPS, localhost, count limit) not found.
Rate limits for OAuth/token endpoints are not stated on the pages read.
Whether a refresh returns a new refresh token is not stated.
Region-specific hosts for the EU service region were not confirmed. The REST API host is assumed to be api.pagerduty.com.
Discovery metadata was not found at identity.pagerduty.com, so no dynamic registration.
Whether a paid plan is needed to publish is not stated. A changelog snippet says Scoped OAuth is available on all plans.
Scope sensitivity levels and consent warnings for unpublished apps are not documented in what was read.
Step 2's link docs.pagerduty.com/developer/integration-developer is a docs page, not the registration form; find the portal page where you create the app.

points.text: Scoped OAuth works on other accounts only after publishing
points.why: Docs: an unpublished Scoped OAuth app works only on the account that created it.

points.text: PagerDuty aims to review within 5 business days
points.why: The review covers testing, documentation and listing details. Reviewer feedback can add rounds.

points.text: An admin on each customer account must install the app
points.why: Users there can't authorize until an admin installs it from the app's install link.

points.text: Classic User OAuth skips review but is legacy and broad
points.why: Classic works across accounts once registered, but its scopes are only read or write.

verdict.summary: Register an app manually; Scoped OAuth apps need PagerDuty review (about 5 business days) and an admin install before other accounts can connect.
